thread:
anya: Heads-up — pulled together a short RFC follow-up for slicing shared dependency debt (libs + runtime glue). TL;DR: propose a 3-layer demarcation (hotpath runtime, near-hot shared libs, cold infra helpers) with explicit ownership and a minimal shim for cross-layer calls.

mike: brief — sounds sensible. can you sketch how this differs from current 'shared-runtime' pattern?

anya: sure — current pattern is a flat shared-runtime package that everyone imports; result: tiny changes ripple, deploy coupling, and hard-to-reason CI. New proposal:
- hotpath/runtime: very small, latency-critical pieces (kv cache, token router) with strict backwards-compatible API.
- near-hot/shared-libs: batching, request shaping, common telemetry helpers. versioned semver, can be deployed behind feature flags.
- cold/infra-helpers: build tooling, scripts, migration code — anything that doesn't affect per-request latency.

ravi: question — how do we enforce the boundaries? compile-time checks? CI lints? runtime guards?

anya: combination. enforce via package visibility rules in repo (we can use CODEOWNERS + enforced import linter). CI will fail on forbidden imports. For runtime compatibility we add a small interface shim in hotpath with very tiny surface (think: getKV(), submitBatch()) and add canary rollout with circuit-breaker.

jess: worried about churn on the hotpath shim itself — if teams keep adding stuff there it becomes the old shared-runtime again. Any guardrails?

anya: yep — we add a 2-step rule: (1) any new API added to hotpath needs a perf microbenchmark + signoff from runtime-owners, (2) default TTL on hotpath API additions: auto-expire in 6 months unless adopted and backfilled with full tests.

mike: adoption plan? Do we need a migration window for existing services that import shared-runtime?

anya: migration plan draft in thread:
- phase 0: add lint and CODEOWNERS, no blocking.
- phase 1 (1 sprint): create hotpath interface shim and move 3-4 highest-throughput calls behind it (canary on staging).
- phase 2 (2-4 sprints): extract near-hot libs into separate modules, update consumers. Provide adapter facades for easy cutover.
- phase 3 (ongoing): move cold helpers to infra repo and deprecate old shared-runtime import.

ravi: rollback strategy? if we hit perf regression when moving a call into the shim?

anya: rollback = feature-flag + route-router fallback to old path. Canary uses 5% traffic ramp with latency SLO alert; if >5% regressed we flip traffic back instantly and revert PR. Also automated latency alarms tied to the deploy.

infra-bot: Deploy-checklist appended: run microbench (bench/run_hotpath.sh), run e2e-sample (scripts/e2e_quick.sh), ensure CODEOWNERS updated.

oliver: curious about ownership model — who signs off on hotpath API additions? runtime-owners? will this be a team or rotating role?

anya: propose runtime-owners group (runtime + infra + 1 service owner) with weekly 30m API review. Rotating reviewers OK but at least one runtime engineer must be present. I'll sketch a draft owner matrix.

mike: can we get a small experiment first — pick one low-risk call (e.g., tenant-metadata read) and run it through the full phase 1 in the next week? low lift and will show tooling gaps.

anya: agreed — volunteer services: enrollment, metrics-ingest. I'll open a short spike PR today and assign reviewers.

jess: please include a clear deprecation note and migration guide in the PR — helps other teams plan.

anya: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — this feels like a pragmatic way to shrink blast radius without a big rewrite.
